title: Joe's All Purpose Wild (house rub and seasoning)
description: The Wild version of Joe's house rub and all-purpose seasoning. Yield: about 4 cups (4 pork butt rubs at 1 cup each). Joe says the ingredient amounts matter most; the yield is just a summary.
steps: Measure everything into a large bowl and whisk until the color is even, breaking up any clumps. Habanero and reaper powders are strong: avoid breathing the dust, and wash your hands (or wear gloves) before touching your eyes.
Store in a glass jar with a tight lid and about 4 cups of space, away from the stove.
Shake the jar before every use (salt and sugar settle).
Pulled pork: about 2 Tbsp per pound, 1 cup for an 8 lb butt. General use: like seasoned salt, lighter than on pork. The sugar can scorch at high heat, so watch the edges.
source: Joe Wuest (house blend), finalized with Head Chef; saved at Joe's request via Head Chef, Nov 14, 2026
notes: Heat level: Wild (about 15,000 SHU est.). The Wild version of Joe's All Purpose (a8a773950216, Mild). Same base as Mild, with habanero as the main heat (about 85% of it), a trace of reaper, and extra sugar to balance. Estimated about 15,000 SHU for the rub (rough calculation from average published chile ranges, not tested). Reflux-friendly: no citric acid, citrus, tomato, or vinegar powders. No mushrooms. Untested as of Nov 14, 2026: if too hot, cut habanero to 3 Tbsp; for more heat, add habanero 1 Tbsp at a time before raising the reaper. Joe doesn't want the reaper to be the main heat. Per Joe's standing rule, habanero dishes are for Joe and Warren only.
